correctness.rationale: A first-round recognizable marked row or column allows all occupied coordinate lines to be recovered after two rounds. For matching marks, first-round marked-neighbor types recover unordered coordinate pairs; the only nonsquare ordering ambiguities are resolved using first-round singleton-mark-neighbor classes with respective counts n-t and m-t, or n-t-1 and m-t-1. Thus stable classes equal pointwise-stabilizer orbits. Exhaustive 70,480 mark selections on six small boards, 2,500 reproducible larger selections, and explicit automorphism enumeration on small boards independently support the proof, while not replacing it.

value.rationale: The full family K_m square K_n has row/column and exceptional equal-axis interchange symmetries. The result completely classifies effects of arbitrary fixed vertices on the stable partition, supplies exact class sizes/counts, and proves a universal sharp two-round refinement bound. This is a motivated structural characterization of a natural finite-model-theoretic invariant rather than isolated small arithmetic.
